scope: Editorial organization-continuity disclosures, separate from counterfactual campaign survival and saved fictional identities.

parties.note: The IEC records cancellation of NNP registration at the party's request effective 3 July 2006. This final legal-registration boundary is distinct from the 2005 dissolution decision. Future templates are counterfactual campaign content, not a claim that the historical NP/NNP remained active after closure.

The DA's history describes a later alliance and organizational transition. The original DP's exact legal integration or ending remains unverified in this roster. Its future templates assume counterfactual campaign survival and must not be read as verified current DP leadership or as DA leaders.

Elections Canada records replacement of the original federal Progressive Conservative registration by the merged Conservative Party on 7 December 2003. This is not provincial PC continuity or a prediction that the original party survives. Its future characters belong only to a counterfactual campaign that retains this organization.

Reform was legally renamed Canadian Reform Conservative Alliance effective 27 March 2000; that rename was not a dissolution. The Alliance registration was then replaced by the merged Conservative Party on 7 December 2003. The intervening Alliance leadership and name-phase presentation are still unreviewed here. Future characters represent counterfactual survival of this game row, not researched current Reform/Alliance leadership.
